Different nociceptive genes are expressed associated with visceral pain symptoms

Different nociceptive genes are expressed associated with visceral pain symptoms. (A-B) Ingenuity pathway analysis software was used to identify the genes (P value <0.1) involved in the nociception in the male (A) and female (B) mice. Blue color represents downregulation and red represents upregulation of identified DEGs. (C-D) Ingenuity pathway analysis relative comparison shows sexual dimorphism in the process of nociception, mechanical nociception, hyperalgesia, and analgesia. (C) IPA suggested strong inhibition of analgesia pathway and activation of nociception and mechanical nociception pathways in male DRG. (D) IPA suggested strong activation of analgesia pathway and mild activation of nociception pathway in female DRG. Mild inhibition of hyperalgesia pathway is also suggested in female DRG

Transcriptome Profiling Suggests Molecular Sexual Dimorphism in Lumbosacral Dorsal Root Ganglia and Sex-specific Mechanisms Underlying Visceral Pain (2026) Sathish Kumar Yesupatham, et al. Physiol Genomics. 2026 Jan 01;58(1). Figure: F5.
